crop.notes: The clipping is the whole of page 8 at low resolution. The Allen item is 'Varying Views: Tom Kelly and Tom Allen Differ on the Big Fight', column 2, with 'Tom Allen's Views' near the middle of the column.

ocr.notes: Transcript covers part of Kelly's remarks, then repeats one sentence hundreds of times and never reaches Allen's section. Allen's paragraph was read only from an enlarged view of the low-resolution page.

title.suggested: Kelly and Allen differ on the Sullivan-Corbett fight

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Post-Dispatch reported that Tom Kelly backed Corbett after his win over Sullivan, while Tom Allen said it was a question of condition and that a properly trained Sullivan could still beat Corbett.

metadata.notes: Masthead reads St. Louis Post-Dispatch, Tuesday, September 13, 1892, page 8.

facts.fact: Allen said Sullivan lost to Corbett because he was out of condition and overweight, and that he did not recognize Corbett as Sullivan's superior
facts.quote: It was all a question of condition. Sullivan was unfit to enter the ring; he was away over-weight and unable to cope with a man of Corbett's agility. I don't recognize Corbett as Sullivan's superior.
